Subject: Re: outage/latency spikes last week (7/27)

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the quick responses on Friday. To summarize from our side: on 7/27 between 09:10–09:45 PDT we saw a sequence of latency spikes culminating in a short outage that caused ~18% of payments to fail in our EU region. The incident had real customer impact and we had to fall back to a queued retry flow to avoid double-charges.

We need three things resolved:
- A clear explanation of root cause and what you’ve changed so this doesn’t repeat.
- Compensation or a credit for the production impact.
- A path to stronger guarantees (higher uptime + tighter latency SLOs) — we want to discuss upgrading to a Premium SLA or other options to reduce risk.

Can we schedule a call this week to review the incident report and an SLA amendment? Priya from our procurement will help with contract steps.

Appreciate the help.

—Tom
Tom Nguyen
Head of Infrastructure | LedgerWorks Inc.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: outage/latency spikes last week (7/27) — technical summary & proposal

Team —

Root cause summary (brief):
- Timeline: 2026-07-27T16:10–16:45Z (equiv ~09:10–09:45 PT).
- Trigger: a coordinated KV cache eviction during a traffic spike triggered a "cache miss storm" on the payments route. This generated high CPU on the inference hosts and increased tail latency; request timeouts hit our backpressure threshold and a subset of requests failed.
- Immediate mitigation applied: increased prefix caching TTL, paused aggressive autoscale down for the affected pool, and enabled temporary additional worker processes.

Proposed permanent customer options:
1) Premium Dedicated Pool (recommended):
   - Dedicated GPU pool with pre-warmed instances for your payment route; isolation eliminates noisy-neighbor risk.
   - SLA: 99.95% monthly uptime; p95 latency <= 200ms for configured route (exclusions for customer-side network).
   - Requirements: minimum 4 reserved GPUs, pre-warm policy (keep X nodes idle), and a configuration to persist KV cache between container restarts.
   - Estimated uplift: $24k/month on top of current usage (approx; final pricing to be part of amendment).

2) Hosted + hardening (less costly):
   - Keep hosted but add KV persistence, increased cache TTLs, and route-level circuit breakers.
   - SLA improvement to 99.9% but not 99.95. Lower cost but some residual co-tenancy risk.

Credit policy note: our Playbook allows a case-by-case credit for incidents with proven platform responsibility. Given the scale of the impact we should offer a consultative credit — suggested starting point: 50% of July hosting fees for the affected routes, with flexibility based on LedgerWorks' procurement ask.

Attachments: incident_report_20260727.pdf (internal write-up, 4 pages) and a draft SLA amendment template (SLA_Amendment_Draft_v1.pdf).

If LedgerWorks wants 99.95 + p95 targets, the Dedicated path is the reliable route. Lead time for provisioning is ~7–10 business days after signed amendment and commitment.

—Neha
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
